A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research on invariant geometric models. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original symmetry assessments, synthetic separation experiments, molecular energy/force predictions, and chirality-related evaluations, including results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds QM9 property-prediction results, alongside revised MD22 and symmetry-assessment results.

M1.justification: GeoNGNN retains its marked subgraphs, inner and outer DisGNNs, distance encoding, and pooling. GeoNGNN-C also retains its orientation-sensitive distances. The explicit GeoNGNN equations in v3 Section 5.1 describe procedures already documented in v2, including Appendix G.

E1.justification: v3 Appendix F.4 adds supervised prediction of 12 QM9 properties, including dipole moment, polarizability, orbital energies, and thermodynamic quantities. QM9 previously appeared only in the symmetry survey. This substantially broadens predictive task coverage; the earlier molecular dynamics, synthetic, ModelNet40, and chirality evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Comparator changes are localized: v3 adds SphereNet and GemNet to the synthetic separation comparison and VisNet-LSRM to MD22, while removing 2F-DisGNN from the efficiency table. The new QM9 comparison includes PhysNet and ComENet, which were not evaluated as baselines in v2.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a QM9 protocol with 110K/10K training/validation examples, batch size 32, and four inner plus one outer layer. The ModelNet40 deviation-error sweep also changes. Appendix F.2 now states a 5 Å MD22 message-passing cutoff, whereas v2 specified 7 Å; however, v3 G.2 still states 7 Å, leaving the actual setting unresolved.

E4.justification: The noise-tolerance analysis is revised: v3 Figure 2 samples additional intermediate ModelNet40 tolerances and changes the plotted symmetry evidence relative to v2 Figure 4. The synthetic separation diagnostic also covers two additional invariant models. The subgraph-radius sensitivity analysis and 3BPA distribution-shift tests are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three-run standard-deviation practice for 3BPA and retain the chirality tables' uncertainty values. No new seed reporting, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: v3 adds the complete QM9 results table and 100% synthetic separation results for SphereNet and GemNet. MD22 DisGNN and GeoNGNN values are revised; for example, GeoNGNN's Ac-Ala3-NHMe energy/force errors change from 0.106/4.9 to 0.093/3.6. These are revised results, not established same-setting gains given the cutoff ambiguity. Symmetry curves also change, while rMD17, 3BPA, chirality, and subgraph-size results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Proposition B.3 asserts inclusion of the distinct-geometric-degree set in the C-asymmetric set; v3 Proposition C.2 replaces this with inclusion in the D-asymmetric set and rewrites the proof. v3 Appendix B.1 independently derives the zero-measure result using polynomial constraints instead of relying on the earlier inclusion argument. Definition 4.1 also excludes zero total mass from barycenter construction.

C1.justification: The central near-completeness and completeness contributions remain. The claimed improvement over Hordan is narrowed from two larger asymmetric sets to one, following the revised set-inclusion result. The abstract and conclusion explicitly emphasize full connectivity and cease presenting downstream competitiveness as a headline contribution, although those evaluations remain in Appendix F.

C2.justification: New Section 5.4 explains why invariant message passing loses local information and why extending completeness to sparse graphs requires stronger conditions than connectivity alone. It also explains the relevance of theoretical completeness when practical implementations use finite cutoffs. Earlier observations about generalization differences and equivariant models' advantages remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies farthest-point sampling for the existing 256-point ModelNet40 preprocessing. Appendix G adds QM9 splits, batch size, subgraph radius, layer counts, and approximately 36–100 training hours on an RTX 4090. Existing implementation details largely remain, although the conflicting MD22 cutoffs reduce reproducibility clarity.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion substantively revises its treatment of GWL's neural realizability and adds positioning against recent equivariant and sparse-graph work, including Cen et al., Wang et al., and Sverdlov and Dym. The comparison with Hordan is narrowed mathematically. v2's discussion of weighted continuous frames and its associated citations is removed; these changes extend beyond relocating related work or updating bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes and rewrites the narrative: related work becomes Section 2, definitions and GeoNGNN exposition are expanded, a dedicated discussion section is added, and the symmetry survey moves into the main experiments. Molecular prediction evaluations move into Appendix F, proofs are reordered, and Appendix G gains an extended NGNN explanation.

P2.justification: v3 adds the QM9 table, a larger counterexample gallery, and an NGNN schematic. It redraws the prior-work set-inclusion diagram, revises the symmetry plots' axes and legends, and restructures comparator columns and highlighting in several tables. Existing displays are also relocated within the reorganized ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: v3 improves theoretical precision by replacing the overstrong C-asymmetry comparison with a D-asymmetry result and a separate zero-measure argument. Its fuller explanation of connectivity assumptions and additional QM9 and separation evidence also help readers assess applicability. These benefits are partly offset by inconsistent MD22 cutoff documentation and removal of the 2F-DisGNN efficiency comparison, supporting a limited net improvement.
